data.title: Tesla Opens Sales Of Autonomous Cybercab for 'Select' Customers — WSJ
data.description:
By Sean O'Kane

Tesla has begun taking orders for personally owned versions of its Cybercab, which has no steering wheel or pedals.

The company said in posts on X on Friday that "select customers are now being invited to purchase Cybercab for personal use" at an estimated purchase price of $29,990. The vehicle requires a $299-per-month subscription to Tesla's autonomy software and a $1,000 nonrefundable deposit.

The autonomous, two-door vehicle was previously only deployed in Tesla's taxi fleet.

The vehicles are estimated to be delivered in December, according to Tesla's posts.

The announcement comes after Tesla and its Chief Executive Elon Musk spent years promising the company would sell fully autonomous vehicles to regular customers. In 2016, Tesla claimed that all vehicles it was making at the time had the hardware necessary to become fully self-driving. In 2019, Musk predicted Tesla would have "over a million robotaxis" on the roads by the following year.

Those promises have yet to materialize, but Tesla has recently made progress toward its autonomous goals. The company has operated "Robotaxi" versions of its Model Y SUV in Austin, Texas since June 2025. That self-driving ride-hailing service has since expanded to other cities in Texas and Florida.

In September, Tesla started adding Cybercabs to the Austin fleet. The gold, two-seater vehicle has no manual driving controls that are required by federal motor vehicle safety standards.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has opened an investigation into whether the Cybercab complies with these regulations. Tesla has told the safety regulator that it believes the Cybercab meets the standards, but the company hasn't publicly explained its position.

Tesla and NHTSA didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The late Friday announcement also signals a possible shift for Tesla's autonomous strategy. On a call with investors in October, Musk said "the vast majority of the Cybercab stuff will be essentially Tesla-owned."

In the social-media posts Friday, the company explained in fine print that the personally owned Cybercabs will only be available to operate "in supported service areas." Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla's head of AI, said in a post that the vehicles will "work unsupervised inside all the same geo locations as" the company's existing Robotaxi service.

Tesla's claim that the Cybercab can only be purchased for personal use means buyers won't be able to immediately make money with the vehicle. The company had previously solicited interest in September for "Cybercab fleet vehicle purchasing." Musk has pitched shareholders on the idea that small fleet owners could manage Cybercabs "like a shepherd tends their flock."

Musk has also promised that customers would be able to add their own Teslas to a larger, autonomous ride-hailing network. On Tesla's October call with investors, Elluswamy said this functionality would come in the second quarter of 2027.

Write to Sean O'Kane at sean.okane@wsj.com

data.title: Why the Microsoft Outage Came at the Worst Possible Time for the Stock — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Callum Keown and Kit Norton

Microsoft has had a rough few days, not quite Nvidia levels of bad, but far from ideal.

A global outage hit the company's Outlook, Teams, and Copilot AI assistant, impacting users across more than 70 countries, according to outage tracker Downdetector. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 services, as well as governments and organizations around the world.

As of Saturday morning, the number of users reporting issues with Microsoft products to Downdetector had dwindled, and Microsoft's service health status webpage was showing that consumer products were operational.

A Microsoft account on X dedicated to posting updates on Microsoft 365 status issues wrote early Saturday morning that the company "completed our efforts to address the underlying issue of the incident and restored service to the remaining impacted customers and regions."

The timing of the outage is particularly inconvenient for Microsoft. Anthropic launched a new suite of office tools on Tuesday and the market saw it as a direct challenge to the tech giant.

Engineers worked to fix the problem for more than a day. At 11:40 a.m. Eastern time Friday, the company again apologized for the disruption and said it was seeing "broad recovery and stability" across its services.

"Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration," Microsoft said.

The company's updates illustrate it was a slog of an effort to restore services. Microsoft said in a status update shortly after 10 p.m. Thursday, more than nine hours after first confirming it was investigating the issue, that changes "applied to improve serviceability" weren't "taking as expected."

Over the intervening hours, however, Microsoft reported improvements in service availability, with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels.

The company has also said the outage was a technical issue and wasn't related to cybersecurity or artificial-intelligence agents. Microsoft will provide a full post-incident report once the company's review is complete.

The stock rose 0.2% to $523.88 on Friday, recovering from a drop of more than 2% in the premarket session.

It's been a tough week for the tech giant. Reports of OpenAI's latest figures suggested that it's some way behind Anthropic in the AI race.

That's bad news for Microsoft, which has a 24% stake in the OpenAI and a much smaller investment in Anthropic.

Investors, however, might be in for some good news next week when the tech company holds its "Ignite" conference. Microsoft is expected to focus on advancements around its cloud platform, Azure, and Copilot.

"We expect the event to reinforce confidence in Microsoft's AI growth narrative," Citi analyst Tyler Radke said in a research note.

Write to Callum Keown at callum.keown@dowjones.com and Kit Norton at kit.norton@barrons.com

data.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Mln Over Android Gallery Data Access
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Italy's privacy regulator has imposed a 805 million euros penalty on Meta Platforms Ireland after finding that the company accessed photos, videos, and related information stored on Android devices without obtaining specific user permission.

The case focuses on a Facebook feature that offered users photo and video suggestions from their phone galleries while they were browsing the app. According to the authority, the feature allowed access to gallery content without providing users with clear information and a separate consent process.

The regulator's investigation began after a consumer complaint and included a technical review of how the feature operated. Following its findings, the authority ordered Meta to switch off the feature by default within 60 days and seek explicit consent before accessing gallery content.

The decision adds to growing scrutiny of how major technology companies handle personal data and user permissions in mobile applications

data.title: Notable tech headlines for the week: Nvidia, Microsoft and Cisco in focus
data.description:
The technology sector grabbed spotlight this week after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO amid reports of extramarital affairs, while a major Microsoft outage disrupted business and government operations across Asia and the U.S.

The tech-focused Nasdaq Composite Index closed in the red on Friday. The top S&P 500 technology gainers and losers for the last week are as follows:

Top Gainers:

  • AMD +18.93%
  • Broadcom +18.16%
  • Monolithic Power Systems +16.81%
  • Arista Networks +15.57%
  • Ciena +15.29%

Top Losers:

  • First Solar -14.79%
  • Nvidia -12.75%
  • Super Micro Computer -6.59%
  • Global Payments -5.68%
  • Accenture -3.87%

Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:

Nvidia CEO Huang resigns

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned on Thursday, the company said, adding that he will be replaced on an interim basis by CFO Colette Kress.

Wall Street brokerages downgraded the stock, with GF Securities became the latest investment firm to lower rating amid concerns about its future.

“As said, the uncertainty is likely to linger and turned out to be a real announcement by Nvidia, considering Jensen’s leadership is crucial to Nvidia (as well as the AI industry).” GF analyst Jeff Pu wrote.

The stock also received downgrades from William Blair, Melius Research, Evercore and KeyBanc, signalling raised concerns about the company's leadership and succession plans. Nvidia stock closed 2% lower on Friday.

Microsoft outage affects Outlook, Teams

Microsoft’s widespread outage affecting services such as Outlook and Teams persisted for hours, disrupting users, businesses, and some government operations across Asia and the U.S. as the company worked to resolve the issue.

The company said it was trying different ways to identify the cause of the problem and get its servers back online. However, it did not have any indication that the outage was caused by malicious activity.

Shares of Microsoft closed in the green on Friday after it said it continues to make 'sustained improvements' in restoring outage.

Cisco in focus after Q1 results

Cisco’s stronger-than-expected earnings and outlook were overshadowed by pressure on hardware margins. The company’s Q1 results featured 43% year-over-year growth in its Networking business segment.

However, analysts were quite positive despite the stock trading lower on Friday.

"The Company is benefitting from a Networking super-cycle that continues to have legs and is driven by five key trends: AI wins with Hyperscalers, Campus refresh and modernization, security-driven upgrades for the AI era, sovereign infrastructure, and hybrid data centers for Enterprises," said BofA analyst Tal Liani.

Other tech headlines include Applied Materials reporting fiscal fourth-quarter results and guidance that topped Wall Street's forecast. Analysts say the results pointed to strong semiconductor equipment demand, AI-related spending, and improving visibility into future factory projects.

CoreWeave is planning to raise at least $4B through an investment-grade loan, with Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group leading the potential financing, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

data.title: SpaceX still planning for Starship launch pad catch Saturday afternoon
data.description:
Key points:
  • An attempt to have SpaceX's upper stage Starship return to earth upright on a launch pad from orbit is still on schedule for around 420p ET Saturday in south Texas even though the company's Super Heavy booster on Friday diverted to an ocean splashdown instead of returning to the launch tower as well.
  • If successful, the Mechazilla launch tower's mechanical arms will "catch" Starship upright, marking the first time ever this has been done for a rocket.
  • At around 2p ET, flight controllers will make a final decision on whether to push ahead with the catch landing or divert to a splashdown off Hawaii.
  • "Starship and its heatshield are healthy as the vehicle continues to orbit Earth after a spectacular start to its mission nearly 7 hours ago," SpaceX said in an X post at 1244a ET. "Teams are continuing to monitor systems ahead of a planned return to launch site catch at Starbase ~22.5 hours after launch."

data.title: Notable analyst calls this week: Nvidia, Broadcom and AMD among top picks
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) closed in the red on Friday, as investors assessed the uncertainty in the broader AI space following the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid reports of extramarital affairs.

Wall Street had a slew of upgrades and downgrades from analysts. Here are some of the major calls for the week:

Nvidia hit with downgrades after Jensen Huang ouster

Nvidia saw a wave of downgrades and price-target cuts this week as analysts warned that the leadership uncertainty could weigh on the stock.

William Blair downgraded Nvidia to Market Perform, saying Huang's likely departure and heightened scrutiny of the company would be a "significant overhang on Nvidia shares in the near term." Evercore downgraded Nvidia to In Line and cut its price target to $186, from $330, citing the prospect of further valuation multiple compression.

Meanwhile, Melius Research cut the stock to Hold, saying it was difficult to assess the situation, comparing it with Hewlett-Packard's leadership crisis in 2010. KeyBanc also downgraded the company to Sector Weight from Overweight, citing increased strategic, organizational, and execution risks.

RBC lowered its PT to $230 from $330 but maintained its Outperform rating, saying a potential change at the top and congressional hearings could create an overhang. Oppenheimer cut it to Market Perform.

“As said, the uncertainty is likely to linger and turned out to be a real announcement by Nvidia, considering Jensen’s leadership is crucial to Nvidia (as well as the AI industry).” GF Securities analyst Jeff Pu wrote and lowered his rating on Nvidia to Hold from Buy, while cutting his price target to $188 from $235.

Earlier in the week, Morgan Stanley removed its top pick label on Nvidia.

Broadcom in focus after Rothschild downgrade

Rothschild & Co. downgraded Broadcom to Neutral, while adding there is potential upside to be had for investors.

“Guidance implies Broadcom trades at 11x FY28 EPS,” said Rothschild analyst Mike Harrison. “But this counts for little when both the quality and the durability of earnings are under scrutiny.

Harrison also lowered his price target on Broadcom to $398 from $595.

“Broadcom’s alignment with Anthropic and OpenAI means the frontier labs need to establish sustained primacy over open models and become self-financing in short order. Beyond this, the market needs reassurance that Google’s customer-owned tooling efforts will not become widespread. The upside potential to Broadcom shares from clearing these hurdles is appreciable but is unlikely to occur quickly,” he added.

AMD upgraded on potential benefit from Nvidia falloutWilliam Blair upgraded AMD to Outperform from Market Perform, citing an opportunity to benefit from the Nvidia related fallout.

“We see a runway for shares to work from here, with Instinct share gains offering additional upside as AMD stays focused on execution while its largest competitor, Nvidia, contends with a growing leadership and regulatory imbroglio,” William Blair analyst Sebastien Naji said.

Naji also pointed out that the Dr. Lisa Su-led AMD is “in the early innings of a multiyear earnings growth trajectory as it continues to execute in server CPUs.”

Palo Alto upgraded ahead of Q1 results

Palo Alto Networks was upgraded to Overweight by KeyBanc Capital Markets ahead of the cybersecurity firm reporting fiscal first-quarter results on Nov. 18.

"We are upgrading shares of PANW to Overweight as we expect security budgets to accelerate through 2027, Palo a leading beneficiary of the trend toward consolidation with strong product offerings in key areas to secure AI and defend against the accelerated AI threat environment, and Palo out-executing many of its cyber peers," analyst Eric Heath wrote and put a $380 price target on Palo Alto shares.

Roblox downgraded to Neutral by Citi

Citi downgraded Roblox to Neutral from Buy, citing concerns over slowing engagement and potential risks to bookings growth. The brokerage maintained its $55 price target.

Citi analyst Jason Bazinet flagged four areas of concern, including waning popularity of Steal An Egg, a lack of emerging hit experiences, potential competition from Grand Theft Auto VI, and uncertainty around booking growth.

Loop Capital upgraded Autodesk to Buy from Hold, citing improving growth expectations.

Baird upgraded Domino's Pizza to Outperform from its previous rating, citing a clearer path to improved same-store sales and franchisee profitability. The brokerage also raised its price target to $400 from $320.

data.title: Swiggy leases 2.6 lakh sq ft Bengaluru office for ₹241 cr over 10 years
data.description:
Swiggy Ltd has leased 2.62 lakh sq ft of office space at Sumadhura Capitol Towers in Whitefield, Bengaluru, with a total rental outgo of approximately ₹241 crore over a 10-year period, according to property data firm Propstack.

The fresh lease covers the building’s third, fourth, fifth and sixth floors, with a chargeable area of 2,62,350 sq ft and a carpet area of 1,94,140 sq ft. The company will pay a monthly rent of ₹1.79 crore, translating into a rental rate of ₹68 per sq ft.

The lease commenced on November 1, 2025, while the registration took place on November 2, 2026. Swiggy has paid a security deposit of ₹10.75 crore for the property.

The rental agreement includes an escalation clause of 15 per cent every three years over the 10-year tenure, which will increase the company’s rental commitments over the lease period.

The property is owned by Sumadhura Capitol Towers Private Ltd, which is the landlord for the transaction.

The lease adds to the office space commitments of the food and grocery delivery company in Bengaluru, where it is headquartered.

data.title: Mercedes-Benz Freezes New Investment In Germany, Puts Factory Closures On The Table As Cost Crisis Deepens
data.description:
With China sales falling 31% in Q3 2026 and its full-year passenger car margin forecast cut to 2-3%, Mercedes-Benz is facing a difficult question - how much of its manufacturing future can Germany still afford?

Mercedes-Benz is no longer treating factory closures in Germany as a distant restructuring possibility. The luxury carmaker has now put the option firmly on the table, freezing all further investments at its German sites as management struggles to bring down manufacturing costs and restore profitability.

In a significant escalation of its confrontation with employee representatives, Mercedes-Benz Chief Production Officer Michael Schiebe confirmed that the company's management board had jointly decided to halt further investments in German locations. The decision was communicated to employees through an internal company interview published on November 12, 2026, according to Reuters.

The message from management was unusually blunt. Britta Seeger, a member of the company's board of management, acknowledged that Mercedes-Benz was now being forced to examine in detail which German facilities it could financially sustain. While management maintains that it wants to avoid factory closures, Seeger conceded that the possibility must now be examined more seriously.

This is a considerable escalation for a company whose identity and industrial history are deeply tied to Germany. It also exposes the uncomfortable reality facing the country's automotive industry, a globally recognised manufacturing reputation is no longer enough to compensate for an increasingly expensive domestic production base.

And Mercedes-Benz's decision is not simply about cutting costs. It reflects a business under pressure from multiple directions, including falling sales in China, intensifying competition, weaker profitability and an increasingly difficult transition towards electric mobility.

China Has Become A Serious Problem For Mercedes-Benz

One of the biggest reasons behind the deteriorating financial picture is China, a market that Mercedes-Benz once relied on heavily to drive sales and profitability.

For years, China was a crucial market for German luxury manufacturers. However, the competitive landscape has changed dramatically. Domestic manufacturers have become increasingly sophisticated, offering feature-rich vehicles, advanced software and competitive pricing. International luxury brands are finding it harder to command the premium they once enjoyed.

Mercedes-Benz's own sales figures underline the problem. The company sold 5,51,900 passenger cars in China in 2025, a decline of 19 per cent compared with the previous year. The situation deteriorated further in 2026. In the third quarter, Chinese passenger car sales fell 31 per cent year-on-year to 86,800 units. For the first nine months of 2026, sales in China were down 29 per cent to 297,000 units.

This is not a minor setback for a company with substantial exposure to the Chinese luxury market. It is a significant deterioration in one of its most important sales regions.

The pressure is also visible in the company's overall passenger car business. Mercedes-Benz Cars delivered 4,07,232 vehicles in Q3 2026, down 7.8 per cent year-on-year. Its revenue declined 5.8 per cent to 22.37 billion euro, while adjusted EBIT fell 50.8 per cent to 560 million euro. The division's adjusted return on sales dropped from 4.8 to 2.5 per cent.

The numbers are particularly concerning because they show that the problem extends beyond sales volumes. Mercedes-Benz is also making considerably less money from the vehicles it sells.

Profitability Has Taken A Hit

The pressure on Mercedes-Benz's finances became even more evident when it revised its 2026 financial guidance on October 28.

The company cut its expected adjusted return on sales for Mercedes-Benz Cars to 2-3 per cent, against its earlier forecast of 3-5 per cent. That is a sharp reduction for a luxury manufacturer that has traditionally relied on premium pricing and healthy margins to support its business.

The wider group is not immune either. Mercedes-Benz reported revenue of 30.7 billion euro in Q3 2026, down 4.5 per cent year-on-year. Adjusted group EBIT declined 15 per cent to 1.78 billion euro. More concerningly, free cash flow from its industrial business fell 87.4 per cent to 172 million euro in the quarter, compared with 1.37 billion euro a year earlier.

For the first nine months of 2026, free cash flow from industrial operations was down 44 per cent to 3.13 billion euro. The company also expects its full-year industrial free cash flow to be significantly below the previous year's level.

The revised outlook is a clear indication that Mercedes-Benz is dealing with more than a temporary slowdown. Its ability to protect margins while funding product development, new technologies and global manufacturing operations is coming under pressure.

US import tariffs have added to the burden. Mercedes-Benz has previously indicated that tariffs cost the company approximately 1 billion euro in profits, further complicating an already difficult operating environment.

German Manufacturing Costs Have Become A Flashpoint

However, the most immediate trigger for the investment freeze is the cost of manufacturing vehicles in Germany. Mercedes-Benz management has argued that the country's production economics are increasingly difficult to justify against alternative manufacturing locations.

According to Schiebe, the cost of an hour of production labour in Germany can be as much as five times higher than at some of the company's facilities in Eastern Europe. That is a substantial cost disadvantage, particularly when manufacturers are competing in price-sensitive segments and facing growing pressure to improve production efficiency.

The comparison with Hungary is especially revealing. Mercedes-Benz's Kecskemét facility has become its largest plant in Europe, while production costs there are reportedly considerably lower than at its German factories. Handelsblatt reported, citing an internal company presentation, that production labour costs at Kecskemét were 75 per cent lower than the average across Mercedes' German plants.

This is precisely the kind of cost difference that makes it difficult for German factories to compete for future production allocations. And Mercedes-Benz is no longer hiding its dissatisfaction with the situation.

The company has been negotiating with its works council and IG Metall, Germany's powerful metalworkers' union, over measures to reduce domestic operating costs. One of management's proposals involves increasing the working week from the collectively agreed 35 hours to 40 hours without additional pay.

The discussions have also involved potential reductions in special employee payments. According to Handelsblatt, Mercedes-Benz is targeting annual savings of around 800 million euro through the proposed measures.

The union has resisted the demands, and negotiations have failed to produce an agreement after months of discussions. The investment freeze is therefore also a pressure tactic. By making future investment conditional on a reduction in labour costs, management is effectively telling employees and their representatives that the existing cost structure cannot continue indefinitely.

But the bigger question is whether the company can resolve its cost problem without damaging the very industrial ecosystem that helped establish its global reputation.

The EV Transition Is Not The Whole Story

Mercedes-Benz's difficulties also need to be viewed against the backdrop of its expensive transition towards electrification.

The company has invested heavily in electric vehicle platforms, battery technology and software while continuing to develop and manufacture internal combustion engine models. Maintaining multiple technology programmes inevitably puts pressure on capital expenditure and production planning.

However, it would be inaccurate to suggest that Mercedes-Benz's electric vehicle business is simply collapsing. Its Q3 2026 results actually showed a 61 per cent increase in battery-electric passenger car sales to 68,428 units. BEV deliveries for the first nine months were up nearly 40 per cent to 1,65,538 units.

The problem is that stronger electric vehicle sales have not been enough to offset the weakness elsewhere in the business, particularly in China. The company is also dealing with lower overall passenger car volumes and substantially weaker adjusted earnings.

In other words, electrification is adding to the complexity of the industry's transformation, but Mercedes-Benz's immediate financial difficulties cannot be blamed on EV adoption alone.

Germany's Automotive Industry Is Facing A Larger Crisis

Mercedes-Benz's decision also raises questions about the future of automotive manufacturing in Germany. The country has long been one of the world's most important automotive manufacturing centres, supported by skilled labour, engineering expertise, established suppliers and globally recognised brands. But those advantages are increasingly being challenged by high operating costs, changing market dynamics and competition from manufacturers with lower-cost production bases.

For Mercedes-Benz, the immediate concern is that the investment freeze could eventually affect the future allocation of new models to German factories. Schiebe has indicated that, without an agreement on cost reductions, new models could instead be produced exclusively outside Germany.

Management has also warned that two factories could face closure if negotiations fail to deliver the required savings. No specific closure decision or final list of affected facilities has been announced.

What This Means For Mercedes-Benz

The immediate investment freeze is a warning to employees, unions and the German automotive industry that Mercedes-Benz is prepared to reconsider the geographical distribution of its manufacturing operations.

The company still has substantial financial resources. Its industrial business reported net liquidity of 31 billion euro at the end of Q3 2026. This is not a company running out of cash. Rather, management is attempting to protect profitability and improve the economics of its manufacturing network before the situation deteriorates further.

But there is an uncomfortable contradiction at the heart of this development. Mercedes-Benz has spent decades building its identity around German engineering and manufacturing. Now, the company is questioning whether manufacturing in its home country makes sufficient commercial sense.

That is a particularly damaging message for Germany's industrial ambitions. If even one of its most recognisable luxury manufacturers is unwilling to commit fresh investment to its domestic factories under the current cost structure, the consequences could extend well beyond Mercedes-Benz.

The company now faces a difficult choice of either securing substantial cost concessions, shift more production abroad or accept that some of its German facilities may no longer have a future.

For a brand that has built much of its global reputation on German engineering, that is a rather stark admission.

Utkarsh Agarwal

BW Reporters

As Editorial Lead of BW Auto World, automotive vertical of BW Businessworld, & Special Correspondent for BW Businessworld, Utkarsh operates at the centre of a rapidly evolving automotive & technology landscape, where the story extends beyond products to business, policy, and shifting consumer behaviour. His work spans product reviews, executive interviews, and feature stories that track and interpret the forces shaping India’s automotive & technology sector. data.title: RBI Gives Paytm In-Principle Nod To Revive Wallet Business
data.description:
Six-month deadline for cybersecurity audit and final clearance will determine when the digital payment service can resume

Paytm has received in-principle approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to restart its digital wallet business through its subsidiary, Paytm Payments Services Limited (PPSL), potentially reopening a payment service that faced restrictions following regulatory compliance concerns. However, the approval does not permit an immediate relaunch. The company must complete an independent systems and cybersecurity audit and submit the findings to the central bank within six months to secure final clearance.

The development follows regulatory action against Paytm Payments Bank, which was barred from accepting fresh deposits and wallet top-ups in early 2024. The RBI cancelled the bank’s licence in April 2026, further separating the banking entity from the payment services business.

Audit Determines Relaunch Timeline

PPSL must undergo an independent systems audit, including a cybersecurity assessment, before it can resume issuing and operating prepaid payment instruments (PPIs). The audit report must reach the RBI within six months. Failure to meet the deadline will result in the in-principle approval lapsing automatically.

The final approval will determine when the company can restart wallet operations. Until then, the regulatory clearance remains conditional, and the financial impact of a potential relaunch is yet to be established.

Why Paytm Wallet Stopped

Paytm’s wallet service was previously operated through Paytm Payments Bank. In early 2024, the RBI restricted the bank from accepting fresh deposits and allowing wallet top-ups following concerns related to compliance with licensing conditions, know-your-customer (KYC) requirements and governance standards.

The restrictions prevented customers from adding money to their existing wallets, disrupting a key part of the company’s digital payments offering.

Payments Bank And Services

Paytm Payments Bank and Paytm Payments Services are separate entities with different functions. The former operated as a banking entity that held deposits and wallet balances before its licence was cancelled. PPSL, a wholly owned subsidiary of One 97 Communications, handles payment solutions and related business services.

The latest in-principle approval applies to PPSL, not the former banking entity. This distinction is central to any revival of the wallet business, which would operate under the applicable regulatory framework for prepaid payment instruments.

What Customers Can Expect

A relaunch following final approval could allow users to load money into digital wallets, maintain balances and make payments for services such as recharges, ticket bookings and bill payments. The company could also explore additional prepaid payment products, subject to regulatory permissions.

Unlike the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), which transfers funds directly between bank accounts without storing money, a prepaid wallet holds money loaded by the user in advance.

The next stage depends on the audit, regulatory review and final authorisation. Until these requirements are met, customers cannot assume that wallet top-ups and services will resume.

data.title: CCI approves Advent International-backed firm's stake acquisition in Yatharth Hospitals
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- The Competition Commission of India (CCI) on Saturday approved the acquisition of a certain shareholding in Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Limited by Rasmalai Limited, an entity indirectly controlled by funds managed or advised by global private equity firm Advent International.

In an official release, the competition regulator said, "The Competition Commission of India (CCI) has approved the acquisition of a certain shareholding of Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd. by Rasmalai Limited."

The proposed transaction involves Rasmalai Limited acquiring a stake in Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Limited.

According to the CCI, Rasmalai Limited is incorporated in Cyprus and is primarily engaged in holding investments. The company currently has no business operations or presence in India.

The regulator said, "The Acquirer is indirectly controlled by investment funds managed and/or advised by Advent International, L.P. and/or its affiliates."

Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Limited operates a network of super-speciality hospitals in India, offering healthcare services, diagnostic facilities and advanced medical procedures across multiple medical specialities.

The approval clears the proposed transaction from the competition regulator's perspective.

data.title: Fed's Collins says gradual rate hikes best to manage economic risks
data.description:
By Michael S. Derby

Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins said on Saturday she supports a steady pace of modest interest rate increases because that path of action better manages economic uncertainties.

The risks on the real side of the economy were "two-sided", she said, which has implications for both the Fed’s job and inflation mandates and argues against taking aggressive action to target high levels of inflation.

In such an environment, "my current view is that a kind of steady, gradual approach for monetary policy is appropriate" Collins told reporters at a conference at her bank.

data.title: 'Are you going to sell fabric cut-pieces?' How Noel Tata defied doubters to build a retail powerhouse
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- "Aap log cut-piece bechnewale hai kya?"

That was the incredulous query from an investor when the Tata Group went into apparel retail 27 years ago, in a country where modern retail was not a concept yet.

On Saturday, Noel Tata, who built and scaled Westside, Zudio and Star Bazaar under the Trent umbrella, recalled the scepticism of the time, when India's consumption engine was yet to turn on, and private labels were unheard of. In the decades that followed, Trent went on to beat at all expectations, the Tata Trusts chairman said at the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit in New Delhi.

"When we first started our first shop, there were only two other shops of significance in India. It was a concept; modern retail was not understood," said Noel, who led Trent as managing director since 1999 and as chairman since 2014. He stepped down last month when he turned 70, in compliance with the Tata Group's retirement policy for non-executive directors.

From betting on private labels at the dawn of modern retail to building Zudio into a 1,000-store chain, Noel Tata's retail strategy centred on product ownership, affordable fashion and India's expanding consumption market.

The retail business has become one of the biggest consumer-facing ventures of Tata Group, with Trent Ltd operating more than 320 Westside stores and over 1,000 Zudio outlets. Zudio alone is on track to generate around Rs.15,000 crore in sales this year, selling nearly 400 million units, Tata said at the Summit.

Noel recalling the journey of building Trent comes at a time when the Tata Trusts he leads have questioned mounting losses at some of Tata Sons' newer businesses such as aviation and e-commerce.

In June 1999, the company formerly known as Lakme Ltd changed its name to Trent and appointed 42-year-old Noel N. Tata to its helm, with a monthly salary that topped out at Rs.1 lakh. At that time, its retail business included four Westside stores in Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, and Mumbai, covering about 80,000 sq ft of shop space.

Twenty-seven years later, Trent's FY2025-26 annual report tells a very different story. Total revenue from operations rose 17.2% to Rs.20,074 crore, and net profit for shareholders rose 11.2% to Rs.1,719.65 crore.

Trent now runs 1,286 stores across 321 cities, with more than 17.7 million sq ft of retail space. That is over 200 times its 1999 footprint. It added 289 stores in the year alone.

The change started with a sale. Lakme's brand names were sold to Hindustan Lever for Rs.110.03 crore, and the company took over its retail subsidiary, Trent (formerly Littlewoods International India), which Noel had managed.

In his latest letter to shareholders, Noel wrote that he remembers opening the first Westside on Bengaluru's Commercial Street in 1998, when modern fashion retail in India was "almost non-existent."

Trent's market cap totalled Rs.1,68,501 crore at the end of Friday, making it the fourth most valuable Tata Group company, behind Tata Consultancy Services Ltd, Tata Steel and Titan Co. Ltd.

The real growth came later. Zudio, the budget brand launched in 2016, had failed as a large store by 2020, before Trent redesigned it. In the next decade, it expanded to 963 stores in 313 cities, including six in the UAE. Westside has 300 stores. Revenue has grown by about 50% a year since FY22, when it was Rs.3,881 crore.

The journey, Tata said, was built on a decision that went against the conventional retail playbook: developing and selling the company's own brands instead of stocking established labels.

"One of the most significant decisions that we took when we first started, which was with Westside, was whether we became a branded retailer or whether we did our own private label brands. And we took the more difficult decision. We said we will do private label," he said.

The choice meant Trent had to take responsibility for designing products, sourcing fabric and managing the entire chain until the merchandise reached customers. Tata described the model as an early direct-to-consumer business in India, giving the retailer control over the product rather than simply acting as a distribution platform for other brands.

The business took time to find its footing. In its initial years, the team believed the Westside format could support about 10 stores across the country. A decade later, expectations had expanded to 50-60 stores, largely across metropolitan markets.

"They worked hard at it for 10 years, with lots of trial and error and patience, and finally, they hit the right note," Saurabh Mukherjea of Marcellus Investment Managers, whose funds own Trent shares, told Mint earlier.

Noel has avoided the acquisition track taken by rivals like Reliance Retail and Aditya Birla Fashion, focusing instead on Trent's own brands. Star, the grocery division, now makes 73% of its revenue from its own labels and runs 84 stores in 12 cities.

How big can Trent get? "Trent has the opportunity to be 10X its size, but don't ask me by when," Noel told Mint in 2024.

Trent's format was designed to offer aspirational products at affordable prices, with stores starting at around 6,000 sq ft and prices ranging from Rs.199 to Rs.999. A decade later, those price points remain unchanged, Tata said.

Zudio also broke away from conventional retail marketing. The chain has neither an e-commerce platform nor a website and has largely stayed away from advertising, relying instead on its physical store network and product quality.

"We've never been on e-commerce and, you know, never done any e-commerce at all," Tata said, adding that the company had not undertaken any advertising apart from a campaign marking the opening of its 1,000th store.

Tata attributed the expansion partly to the growing reach of consumption in India, particularly in smaller cities. Demand for better products was no longer restricted to metros, with tier-II and tier-III towns increasingly contributing to the consumption story. He also credited the broader expansion of India's economy for the opportunity, saying the growth in consumption was visible across socio-economic categories and geographies.

data.title: Earnings Scoreboard: All 10 reporting firms beat EPS estimates across seven sectors; 8 grow Y/Y profits
data.description:
Earnings season continues with 10 companies reporting quarterly results across utilities, industrials, financials, energy, communication services, materials, and information technology.

Earnings Roundup:

Bottom Line: Out of the 10 companies reporting, all 10 exceeded EPS expectations. Notably, 8 firms posted year-over-year earnings growth (while 1 declined and 1 had no prior-year comparison).

Top Line: Out of the 10 companies reporting, 8 exceeded revenue expectations, while 2 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, 8 firms posted year-over-year revenue growth.

Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

Constellation Energy : advanced just over 10% post-earnings after reporting Q3 adjusted operating earnings of $5.06 per share, beating the $3.88 consensus estimate, alongside revenue of $9.55B (+45.4% Y/Y). Management raised and narrowed its full-year adjusted operating earnings guidance to $12.50–$12.80 per share, citing Calpine accretion, strong commercial performance, and higher PJM capacity prices.

Ferguson Enterprises : climbed 11.22% post-earnings after reporting Q3 revenue of $9.03B (+9.5% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $310M, while non-GAAP EPS of $3.43 topped forecasts by $0.14. Growth was driven by 7.0% organic expansion and 2.7% from acquisitions, prompting management to raise its calendar 2026 net sales outlook to ~7% growth and narrow its adjusted operating margin target to 9.6%–9.8%.

KKR & Co. : climbed 2.0% post-earnings after delivering Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.78, surpassing the $1.58 consensus estimate, while revenue reached $2.61B (+8.8% Y/Y). Results were bolstered by record fee-related earnings of $1.32B and strong returns in infrastructure (+4%) and alternative credit (+3%), with the firm expecting to return over $40B to clients in 2026.

NRG Energy : gained just over 10% alongside a broader utility rally after reporting Q3 revenue of $9.47B (+24.0% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $180M, and non-GAAP EPS of $4.68, topping forecasts by $1.65. Management reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $7.90–$9.90 and projected 2027 adjusted EPS of $8.05–$10.05 ($9.05 midpoint).

Occidental Petroleum : rose 2.04% post-earnings after reporting better-than-expected Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.91 (beating by $0.44), even as revenue of $6.56B missed consensus estimates. A 32.5% Y/Y jump in average realized oil prices to $85.91/bbl helped offset a 2.5% dip in global production to 1.43M boe/day caused by maintenance and Gulf of Mexico curtailments, with Q4 output guided to 1.43M–1.47M boe/day, with output from the Permian Basin expected to ‌come in at 820K-840K boe/day.

Take-Two Interactive Software : rose 8.31% post-earnings in reaction to its FQ2 results and GTA 6 update, despite total net bookings falling 18% Y/Y to $1.60B (missing the $1.66B estimate) and EPS coming in at $1.00. Looking ahead, the company guided FY27 revenue to $8.0B–$8.2B and EPS to $0.57–$0.75, trailing consensus estimates.

TransDigm Group : rose 0.55% post-earnings as a soft profit outlook overshadowed a Q4 beat, with revenue rising 22.6% Y/Y to $2.99B (beating by ~$40M) and adjusted EPS of $12.44 topping the $12.21 consensus. While management projected FY27 revenue of $11.95B–$12.15B above estimates, its FY27 adjusted EPS forecast of $47.09–$47.94 fell short of the $48.66 consensus amid higher borrowing costs.

Vylor Inc. : fell 0.06% post-earnings after reporting Q3 revenue of $938M (-0.6% Y/Y), beating consensus estimates by $19.94M, while non-GAAP EPS of -$0.42 topped expectations by $0.10. Supported by continued technology adoption, the company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 outlook for adjusted pro forma operating EBITDA of ~$2.8B and EPS of $2.25–$2.35 vs. consensus of $2.38.

Applied Materials : rose 1.4% in extended trading after reporting Q4 FY2026 revenue of $10.41B (+53% Y/Y), surpassing the $10.3B estimate, while adjusted EPS of $4.16 beat the $4.05 consensus. Fueled by strong AI-driven semiconductor demand, the company guided Q1 FY2027 revenue to $10.6B–$11.6B ($11.1B midpoint) and adjusted EPS to $4.15–$4.55 ($4.35 midpoint), both above Street forecasts.

Cisco Systems : perked up 2% in early post-market trading after Q1 FY2027 revenue rose 24% Y/Y to $18.5B (beating the $18.13B estimate) and adjusted EPS of $1.40 topped the $1.33 consensus. Performance was propelled by 43% Y/Y growth in networking ($11.13B), prompting Cisco to raise its FY2027 adjusted EPS outlook to $5.47–$5.52 and revenue guidance to $74.8B–$75.8B, with AI hyperscaler revenue expected to reach $9B.

Earnings next week:

As earnings season rolls on, investors are tracking key reports across communication services, consumer discretionary, consumer staples, and information technology.

Key reports to watch include The Walt Disney Company , The Home Depot , Lowe's Companies , Ross Stores , The TJX Companies , Target Corporation , Tyson Foods , Walmart , NVIDIA Corporation , Palo Alto Networks , Intuit , Keysight Technologies , and Everpure .

data.title: Hungary recovers $20 million cash in probe of Orban minister
data.description:
By Gergely Szakacs

Hungarian authorities have recovered nearly $20 million in cash, some buried in forests or hidden in farm buildings and warehouses, in a bribery investigation into Miklos Sesztak, a minister under former leader Viktor Orban.

Prime Minister Peter Magyar ousted Orban after 16 years in power in an April election, pledging to mend ties with the European Union strained by years of disagreements under Orban, and to launch a sweeping investigation into allegations of graft.

The clampdown is part of an anti-graft drive the centre-right Magyar has dubbed "Operation Purgatory", which 70% of respondents rated as "very important" in a survey by the pollster Median carried by news website HVG this week.

"During searches, investigators found large amounts of cash buried in forests, hidden in farm buildings, warehouses and a residential property, and stored in a high-value safe in a secluded location," the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office said late on Friday.

Finance Minister Andras Karman said it took a dozen State Treasury workers eight hours using banknote counters to count the cash that had been retrieved.

Magyar said the recovered cash signalled the end of what he described as a "mafia" led by Orban's right-wing Fidesz party and his Christian Democrat allies during Orban's 16-year rule.

Fidesz wrote in a Facebook post that it hoped Sesztak was not connected to the cash.

"Since the change of regime, every lawmaker in Hungary has sworn an oath to abide by and enforce the law. Fidesz-KDNP (Christian Democrats) cannot associate itself with anyone who fails to do so. We trust that the images published by the NVVH (asset recovery office) have nothing to do with Miklos Sesztak," Fidesz wrote.

Sesztak — Orban's development minister from 2014 to 2018 — has denied wrongdoing. His lawyer, Gabor Papp, did not respond to a request for comment on the recovery office's statement. But he told local news website Telex the seized cash did not belong to Sesztak, a member of parliament's Economic and Energy Affairs Committee. He added that the bribery case also involved other suspects.

FORMER MINISTER FACING CALL TO RELINQUISH HIS MANDATE

But Bence Retvari, parliamentary group leader of the Christian Democrats, said Sesztak, the party's vice chair, should relinquish his parliamentary mandate as he seeks to clear his name.

"This is an individual criminal case, and the criminal proceedings must be kept strictly separate from our political community," Retvari said on Facebook.

"Peter Magyar wants to use it to portray the entire right as a criminal organisation. We reject this in the strongest possible terms!"

In separate investigations, two former ministers from Orban's government and former central bank chief Gyorgy Matolcsy are under arrest over graft accusations. They have denied wrongdoing.

Authorities have also detained Orban's brother in a people-smuggling case that the former leader has dismissed as an act of political revenge.

Gabor Torok, a political scientist, said the images of the cash were so vivid they likely spelled doom for Fidesz, whose support fell by half from its pre-election level to 16% of voters in November, a Median survey showed.

($1 = 330.82 forints, 0.9074 euros)

data.title: Who is Rene Haas? Arm CEO emerges as potential Nvidia chief after Jensen Huang's exit; what makes him a frontrunner?
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Nvidia has reportedly approached Arm Holdings chief executive Rene Haas as it explores potential successors to Jensen Huang, according to a Financial Times report.

Haas, who spent seven years at Nvidia before joining Arm in 2013, is among several names being reportedly considered for the top job at the US chipmaker.

However, there is no certainty that Haas will be offered the position or agree to take it up.

Nvidia's board has said it is still in the process of selecting an executive search firm and has not formally approached any potential candidates.

The reported development comes amid speculation over Nvidia's leadership transition, with some employees reportedly urging the board to reconsider its decision and bring back Huang.

Rene Anthony Andrada Haas, 64, is an American technology executive who has led Arm Holdings since February 2022.

He is also a member of the British chipmaker's board and a director of its parent company, Japan's SoftBank Group.

Haas has more than three decades of experience in the semiconductor and computing industries.

Before taking charge of Arm, he spent seven years at Nvidia, where he rose to become vice president and general manager of its computing products business.

He joined Arm in 2013 and went on to hold several senior leadership positions before being appointed its chief executive in 2022.

His familiarity with Nvidia's operations, engineering culture and business strategy, combined with his experience running a publicly listed semiconductor company, has made him a potential contender for the role.

Under Haas, Arm has expanded its focus beyond its traditional strength in mobile phone processors to areas such as artificial intelligence, data centres, automotive computing and high-performance processors.

One of his major milestones was overseeing Arm's return to public markets through its Nasdaq initial public offering (IPO) in September 2023. The listing was among the biggest stock market debuts of that year.

Arm does not typically manufacture chips itself. Instead, it develops processor architectures and intellectual property that other companies license to design semiconductors for smartphones, computers, data centres and connected devices.

Its technology is used across a broad range of computing products, giving Haas experience in an industry that is increasingly central to the global AI boom.

Nvidia's board is searching for a permanent successor after co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as president and chief executive on November 12.

The company appointed its chief financial officer, Colette Kress, as interim CEO while it considers internal and external candidates.

The leadership crisis followed reports about Huang's extramarital relationships, including one involving Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whom US intelligence reportedly suspects of being a spy.

The espionage allegation has not been independently established, and Beijing has denied it.

The board has said it is selecting an executive search firm and has not formally engaged any potential candidates. This is an important distinction from the Financial Times report that it approached Haas.

While the board considers potential successors, a section of Nvidia's workforce has reportedly called for Huang to return.

According to a report by technology publication Wired, an internal post by a longtime Nvidia engineer urging the board to take employee sentiment into account has attracted more than 1,600 comments. Several employees reportedly called for Huang's reinstatement.

Billionaire Elon Musk also said on X that a petition was being organised to bring Huang back and that he would sign it. It remains unclear whether Musk was referring to the internal employee campaign.

Whoever takes over from Huang will inherit a company at the centre of the global artificial intelligence boom, but also one facing mounting geopolitical, regulatory and competitive pressures.

Huang led Nvidia for more than three decades, overseeing its transformation from a graphics-processing company into a dominant supplier of AI chips.

His role extended beyond product development to strategic investments, relationships with technology companies and negotiations surrounding semiconductor exports to China.

The next chief executive will have to navigate growing scrutiny from US lawmakers over advanced chip exports to China, intensifying competition in AI computing and the challenge of sustaining Nvidia's position in the global semiconductor market.

data.title: Jensen Huang Is Out. What Happens to Nvidia Stock Now?
data.description:
Editor’s Note: Jensen Huang’s sudden departure from Nvidia has left investors with some big questions. Is the AI chip giant still a buy? And what happens to the AI boom without one of its most influential leaders? My colleague Louis Navellier has some thoughts. But he also sees a much bigger shift taking place on Wall Street – one he explored during his recent Fed Warning 2027 presentation.

Today, Louis explains whether he’s still holding Nvidia, where Wall Street’s money is moving, and why yesterday’s market leaders may not be tomorrow’s winners. He’ll also talk more about his Fed Warning 2027 and how to prepare for what comes next.

What a difference a week makes, folks.

Just a few days ago, Jensen Huang was the face of the AI Revolution. As CEO of Nvidia Corp. (NVDA), he was one of the most powerful figures in technology, with investors hanging on his every word.

Today, he’s out of a job.

His shocking resignation has sent shock waves through Wall Street, raising serious questions about Nvidia’s future – and what comes next for the AI boom.

But here’s something you may find interesting.

This past Thursday, I shared my special Fed Warning 2027 presentation.

We talked about the market’s narrowing list of winners, the rotation taking place on Wall Street, and where I see the biggest opportunities emerging as we head into 2027.

I also unveiled something I’ve been working on for quite some time: my brand-new investment service, Prime Portfolio.

In fact, last weekend, I personally selected the first 25 stocks for my new portfolio.

And Nvidia wasn’t one of them.

Now, don’t misunderstand me. Even after Huang’s resignation, I still believe Nvidia’s has tremendous earnings power, and I’ll be watching its upcoming earnings report closely.

But the market is rotating, and yesterday’s winners won’t necessarily lead tomorrow.

That’s precisely why I built Prime Portfolio. It goes well beyond stock picks, with tools to help you allocate your money, monitor your holdings, and know when to make a change.

Today, I’ll explain what Huang’s departure means for Nvidia, why the market’s rotation is so important, and how my new service is designed to help you stay on the right side of it.

What Jensen Huang’s Resignation Means for Nvidia Stock

I’ll admit, I didn’t see Jensen Huang’s resignation coming.

On Monday, I expected the Nvidia Board of Directors and the U.S. government to eventually clear Huang of wrongdoing. As recently as Wednesday, I remained confident he would weather the storm.

Clearly, things changed in a hurry.

Reports of Huang’s relationship with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence have been raising questions about whether sensitive information had been compromised for a few days. Then on Wednesday night, news of a second extramarital affair emerged. By Thursday morning, Huang had resigned, and longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress was named interim CEO.

There are still plenty of unanswered questions:

  • Was sensitive information exposed? 
  • What happens to Nvidia’s relationship with China? 
  • And who can replace the visionary leader who built Nvidia into the dominant force in AI chips?

Should Investors Sell Nvidia Stock?

But here’s what I want you to remember. Nvidia’s earnings power didn’t disappear overnight.

Before all this drama, analysts were forecasting third-quarter sales growth of about 91% and earnings growth of 90%. Those are stunning numbers. And while the leadership shakeup creates uncertainty, Nvidia still has its technology, its customers, and enormous demand for the chips powering the AI Revolution.

The company is scheduled to report earnings on November 17. I’ll be paying especially close attention to management’s guidance and whether analysts begin cutting their estimates.

For now, I’m recommending that investors hang on to their Nvidia shares while we assess the situation.

The bottom line: I don’t make investment decisions based on shocking headlines alone. I follow the sales, earnings, and underlying strength of a business.

And right now, there’s another important development taking place on Wall Street that investors shouldn’t overlook.

Why Nvidia Isn’t the Only Stock Investors Should Be Watching

You see, folks, the market’s rotation didn’t begin with Jensen Huang’s resignation.

It’s been underway for some time.

Take IREN Ltd. (IREN), for example.

On November 5, the AI neocloud company reported strong top-line growth, with revenue jumping 66% to $228.3 million as AI cloud sales nearly tripled. However, it also posted a steep $263 million net loss – missing earnings estimates – while warning of rising costs and a delay to its $4 billion annual recurring revenue (ARR) target.

Meanwhile, in 2026, its Stock Grader rating has plunged from an A to an F.

That’s a dramatic reversal. And it’s a reminder that even the hottest stocks can fall out of favor when the underlying numbers change.

That’s why I follow the data rather than getting caught up in the hype.

Where Wall Street’s Money Is Moving Now

Meanwhile, some of the best opportunities are emerging outside the familiar AI names – and in other sectors. Just look at how the major stock market sectors have performed over the past six months.

Healthcare and Financial Sector stocks have led the way, while Technology and Communication Services have struggled. Even Energy has outperformed Technology and Communication Services over this period.

And that rotation is already reflected in my new Prime Portfolio.

In fact, a good portion of my first 25 picks are energy companies. I’ve also included three healthcare stocks.

These aren’t random choices. They’re the result of my quantitative system identifying companies with strong earnings prospects and other characteristics I look for in winning stocks.

That’s what rotation is all about: finding what’s working – and positioning yourself for what comes next.

And it’s the driving force behind the 25 stocks I just selected for Prime Portfolio.

How to Position Your Portfolio for the Next Market Leaders

Folks, I’ve spent more than 40 years studying the stock market. And if there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s that the market never stands still.

I didn’t predict Jensen Huang’s departure. And I can’t tell you what the next shocking headline will be.

But I know the market will keep changing, money will keep sloshing around – and yesterday’s winners won’t always lead tomorrow.

That’s why I built Prime Portfolio for markets like this.

My goal is simple: Assemble the crème de la crème of stocks based on what my quantitative system is telling me. Then, as market conditions change, make the adjustments needed to stay focused on what’s working.

data.title: Saudi Water Authority cancels Va Tech Wabag’s 300 MLD desalination project in Yanbu
data.description:
Water technology company Va Tech Wabag said on Saturday that the Saudi Water Authority had cancelled an order for a 300 MLD mega seawater desalination plant earlier awarded to Wabag.

“Subsequent to the award, the company had completed the necessary formalities and executed the contract, which was submitted to the customer (Saudi Water Authority) for their counter-signature and formal commencement of the project. However, the customer has now notified all tender participants through the Etimad portal (Electronic Government Procurement and Tendering Platform of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia) that the said tender has been cancelled due to internal reasons attributable to the customer,” Va Tech Wabag said.

Wabag said it is in the process of approaching the customer to understand the reason in better detail and the next course of action.

The order is related to the design, engineering, supply, construction, and commissioning of a 300 MLD Mega Desalination plant at Yanbu, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

data.title: Dividend stock to buy: TD Power shares rally 369% in 3 years, more upside ahead? Check target price before record date
data.description:
New Delhi, Nov. 14 -- Shares of TD Power systems will remain in focus in the coming week because of the upcoming dividend record date. The company scrip ended last week with 10.56% gain, which coincided with the announcement of second quarter results for the financial year 2026-27.

TD Power Systems share price closed 1.85% higher during Friday's trading session. Its share price value has surged 10.56% over the last one month. Strong Q2FY27 results, robust order book, and upgraded guidance have strengthened the outlook for the company, according to SBI Securities which sees 14.8% upside potential in the stock.

Strong performance in the September quarter, aided by margin expansion, has strengthened the case for TD Power Systems.

Management confirmed that this inflow is demand-driven and not supply-pushed. Furthermore, the vast majority of the pending order book is scheduled for execution over the next 12 months.

Dedicated power for AI and hyperscale data centres, grid stability and grid stabilisation equipment, expansion in baseline primary power generation and a worldwide shift towards decarbonisation are among key contributors in boosting TD Power Systems' order book growth.

SBI Securities gave 'Buy' recommendation for the stock with a target price of Rs.732 per share. "At CMP of Rs.638, the stock trades at FY27E/FY28E P/E of 51.8x/41.8x respectively," read SBI Securities report.

The company has fixed Wednesday, November 18, as the record date to determine the eligibility of shareholders for dividend. Its board of directors approved Rs.0.65 per equity share dividend with a face value of Re 1 each.

The stock closed 1.85% higher at Rs.637.55 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.20,493.97 crore on Friday, November 13. Its share price value has surged 10.56% in one week, 89.42% in 2026 so far, 63.97% in one year, and 368.87% (approx 369%) in three years.
